classes.label: Brain Monitoring with Information Technology (BrainIT) Group
classes.definition: An open collaborative international network aimed at improving standards for the collection of neurointensive care data on patients with traumatic brain injury.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-0
1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-2
1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-5
classes.evidence: The Brain Monitoring with Information Technology (BrainIT) group approach is to foster free and open collaboration towards raising standards for collection and analysis of data from patients with traumatic brain injury.
aliases: Brain Monitoring with Information Technology (BrainIT) group

classes.label: Core Dataset
classes.definition: A defined set of data elements to be collected from all centres regardless of specific project aim.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-0
1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-2
1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-5
classes.evidence: The aim was to define a minimum or core dataset to be collected from all head injured patients which would be common to all future research projects.

classes.label: Traumatic Brain Injury
classes.definition: A type of brain injury resulting from external mechanical forces, often leading to significant morbidity and mortality.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-0
1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-5
classes.evidence: The successful completion of this 'proof of concept' phase will create a network of centres capable of multi-centre computer based standardised collection of validated, high resolution, well documented management and monitoring data from patients with Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI).

classes.label: Head Injury
classes.definition: An injury to the head that can result in serious consequences and is a leading cause of death in young males.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-0
classes.evidence: Head injury is a leading cause of death in young males and survivors have serious and long term morbidity.

classes.label: CPP
classes.definition: A physiological parameter measuring the pressure of blood flow to the brain, calculated as Blood Pressure minus Intracranial Pressure.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-0
1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-5
classes.evidence: Over the last few years an interest in Cerebral Perfusion Pressure (CPP) targeted therapy for head injured patients has developed with a number of observational studies indicating that a Cerebral Perfusion Pressure (CPP) of 70 mmHg appears to be a critical value.

classes.label: Monitoring Data
classes.definition: Data collected continuously to assess the physiological status of patients, particularly in neuro-intensive care settings.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-0
1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-5
1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-6
classes.evidence: the technical aims of the group are to collect both monitoring and non-monitoring core dataset elements from multiple centers using bedside.

classes.label: Health Care Technology
classes.definition: Innovative tools and methods used to improve patient care and outcomes, particularly in the context of brain injury.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-0
classes.evidence: The Brain Monitoring with Information Technology (BrainIT) network provides an infrastructure for monitoring similar to that required by the Pharmaceutical industry in the conduct of trials of new drugs.

classes.label: Demographic and Clinical Information
classes.definition: Data elements related to patient demographics and clinical status collected once per patient.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-2
classes.evidence: Demographic and Clinical Information group contains data elements which are only collected once per patient and as such are not considered time-series data.

classes.label: Minute by Minute Monitoring Information
classes.definition: Data collected at minute intervals regarding a patient's physiological parameters.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-2
classes.evidence: Minute by Minute monitoring information.

classes.label: Intensive Care Management Information
classes.definition: Information related to the management of patients in intensive care settings.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-2
classes.evidence: Intensive care management information.

classes.label: Secondary Insult Treatment Information
classes.definition: Data concerning treatments administered to address secondary insults in patients.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-2
classes.evidence: Secondary insult treatment information.

classes.label: GCS Assessment
classes.definition: A scale used to assess a patient's level of consciousness and neurological status.

1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-3
classes.evidence: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores at both pre-neurosurgical hospital admission and at admission to the hospital with Neurosurgery.

classes.label: Computed Tomography (CT) Scan
classes.definition: An imaging technique used to visualize internal structures of the body, particularly the brain.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-2
classes.evidence: Computed Tomography (CT)-Scan data and worst Computed Tomography (CT)-Scan information is collected.

classes.label: Extended 8-point Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOSE)
classes.definition: A scale used to measure the outcome of patients after a brain injury.

classes.evidence: Consensus was achieved to collect from all patients the Extended 8-point Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOSe) at 6 months post discharge from the neurosurgical centre.

classes.label: Heart Rate
classes.definition: A physiological parameter indicating the number of heartbeats per minute, monitored using Electrocardiogram (ECG) or Pulse Oximetry.

classes.label: Respiration Rate
classes.definition: A physiological parameter measuring the number of breaths taken per minute, monitored using impedance plethmography or ventilator.

classes.evidence: Respiration Rate (sources: impedance plethmography or ventilator)

classes.label: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP)
classes.definition: The pressure of circulating blood on the walls of blood vessels, an important vital sign in patient monitoring.

1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-5
classes.evidence: the inter-centre differences in location of the 'zero' pressure reference site for the Blood Pressure (BP) transducer.

classes.label: ICP
classes.definition: The pressure inside the skull, monitored to assess brain health, particularly in patients with neurological conditions.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-3
1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-5
classes.evidence: a lack of standardisation between centres on the site of Intracranial Pressure (ICP) monitoring (intraventricular vs intraparenchymal vs subdural)

classes.label: Sao2
classes.definition: A non-invasive method used to measure the oxygen saturation level of the blood.
provenance: 1.Pipre 2003 - The BrainIT group concept and core dataset definition::chunk-3
classes.evidence: Pulse Oximetry (SaO2)

classes.label: Temperature
classes.definition: A physiological parameter indicating the body temperature, monitored through various sources.

classes.evidence: Temperature (sources: rectal=oesophageal= bladder=skin)

classes.label: CVP

classes.label: EtCO2

classes.label: Jugular Venous Oxygen Saturation

classes.label: Brain Temperature

classes.label: Intensive Care Unit
classes.definition: A specialized department in a hospital that provides intensive treatment and monitoring for critically ill patients.
classes.evidence: The Intensive Care Unit (ICU) domain generates large volumes of patient data which can be used in medical research.

classes.label: Patient Data
classes.definition: Information collected from patients, which can be recorded manually and/or automatically in medical settings.
classes.evidence: Increasing use of patient monitoring equipment in medicine is generating large repositories of patient data, which are recorded manually and/or automatically.

classes.label: Data Quality Assessment
classes.definition: The accuracy and reliability of data collected in medical settings, which is crucial for medical decision making.
classes.evidence: Trusting this data is important: along with being used for medical decision making, the data is often stored for offline analysis.

classes.label: Error Rates
classes.definition: The frequency of inaccuracies found in medical data, which can vary significantly.
classes.evidence: However, error rates of between 2.3% and 26.9% are common.

classes.label: Sepsis
classes.definition: A life-threatening condition that arises when the body's response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.
classes.evidence: if the patient was suffering from sepsis at the same time, then the value may actually be a symptom of that disorder.

classes.label: Rdf
classes.definition: Resource Description Framework, a standard model for data interchange on the web.
classes.evidence: Our approach consists of three stages: converting the medical data into RDF.

classes.label: Provenance Information
classes.definition: Data that provides context about the origin and history of the medical data collected.
classes.evidence: optionally annotating the data with provenance information

classes.label: Linked Open Data
classes.definition: A method of publishing structured data so that it can be interlinked and become more useful through semantic queries.
classes.evidence: we intend to contribute to the Linked Open Data cloud.

classes.definition: An individual receiving medical care or treatment.
classes.evidence: the pd:Patient as a ssn:FeatureOfInterest

classes.definition: A defined period during which medical observations are recorded.

classes.definition: A recorded observation of a specific parameter and its value.
classes.evidence: define pd:Reading as a subclass of ssn:ObservationValue

classes.label: Parameter
classes.definition: A measurable characteristic or variable being observed in a patient.
classes.evidence: pd:Parameter (representing things that were recorded) as a subclass of ssn:Property

classes.label: Observation
classes.definition: A recorded measurement or assessment made during patient care.
classes.evidence: pd:Timepoint as a subclass of mo:ObservationCollection

classes.label: Machine
classes.definition: A device used in medical evaluations to collect data.
classes.evidence: defined mms:Machine as a subclass of ssn:Platform

classes.label: Sensor
classes.definition: A device that detects and measures physical properties.
classes.evidence: various subclasses of ssn:Sensor for the different types of sensors on the machine

classes.label: Provenance
classes.definition: Information describing the origin and history of data.
classes.evidence: annotating the patient observations with provenance

classes.label: Configuration
classes.definition: Settings and parameters that define how data is recorded.
classes.evidence: knowledge about how the sensors were configured to record the data

classes.label: Assessment
classes.definition: An evaluation of patient data against predefined criteria.
classes.evidence: a single temporary assessment dataset is created consisting of the patient observations RDF dataset

classes.label: Error
classes.definition: An identified issue with a recorded value in patient data.
classes.evidence: If a value is identified as an error it is annotated with 'Possible Error' (PoE) or a 'Probable Error' (PrE)

classes.label: Missing Data Rule
classes.definition: A rule that identifies conditions under which data readings are considered missing based on specific criteria.
classes.evidence: Missing If, for every sequential pair of readings, the time period PrE Data 3 between them does not equal the sampling rate

classes.label: Acceptable Range
classes.definition: A set of conditions that define the acceptable limits for recorded values in clinical monitoring.
classes.evidence: Acceptable If the recorded value is less than the min. acceptable value PrE Range 1

classes.label: Medical Disorders
classes.definition: A category of conditions that may be associated with abnormal recorded values in clinical data.
classes.evidence: Medical If the recorded value is outwith its acceptable range AND is associated with a symptom of a disorder

classes.label: Hypertension
classes.definition: A medical condition characterized by elevated blood pressure, which may affect clinical data readings.
classes.evidence: a number of readings identified by Acceptable Range Rules 1 & 2 may have been affected by hypertension (91%)

classes.label: Hypotension
classes.definition: A medical condition characterized by abnormally low blood pressure, which may influence clinical data readings.
classes.evidence: a number of readings identified by Acceptable Range Rules 1 & 2 may have been affected by hypotension (85.6%)

classes.label: Noradrenaline
classes.definition: A medication used in critical care to manage blood pressure, which may affect clinical data readings.
classes.evidence: queries for effects of noradrenaline

classes.label: Adrenaline
classes.definition: A medication used in critical care that can influence physiological parameters, impacting clinical data readings.
classes.evidence: queries for effects of adrenaline

classes.label: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure
classes.definition: The pressure gradient driving blood flow to the brain, calculated as Blood Pressure minus Intracranial Pressure.
classes.evidence: Cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP 1/4 Blood Pressure (BP)-ICP) monitoring is a good example.

relations.evidence: if the patient was suffering from sepsis at the same time, then the value may actually be a symptom of that disorder.

relations.label: has reading

relations.evidence: Each Timepoint is associated with a set of Readings

relations.label: produces

relations.evidence: the ssn:Sensing process that is implements, the ssn:Property it observes

relations.label: records

relations.evidence: the machines used in our medical evaluation

relations.label: annotates

relations.label: configures
relations.definition: Indicates how a machine is set up to record data.

relations.label: evaluates

relations.label: affects
relations.definition: Indicates that abnormal recorded values may be associated with symptoms of medical disorders.
relations.evidence: If the recorded value is outwith its acceptable range AND is associated with a symptom of a disorder

relations.label: affects
relations.definition: Indicates that abnormal recorded values may be associated with effects of treatments administered.
relations.evidence: If the recorded value is outwith its acceptable range AND is associated with an effect of a treatment AND that treatment was administered previous to that value

relations.label: monitors
relations.definition: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure is monitored in patients with Traumatic Brain Injury to assess brain perfusion.
relations.evidence: Cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP 1/4 Blood Pressure (BP)-ICP) monitoring is a good example.

relations.label: supports
relations.definition: Health Care Technology supports the management and treatment of patients with Traumatic Brain Injury.
relations.evidence: the Brain Monitoring with Information Technology (BrainIT) network provides a more standardised and higher resolution data collection mechanism for research groups, organisations and the device industry to conduct multi-centre trials of new health care technology in patients with traumatic brain injury.

relations.label: affects
relations.definition: Data Validation affects the quality and reliability of Health Care Technology assessments.
relations.evidence: we have achieved a key first step in this process by defining minimum data validation standards and have developed a mechanism for checking the validity of data against original documentation.

relations.label: has admission data
relations.definition: Every patient can be linked to their admission data.
relations.evidence: the incidence of serious head injury is estimated at 1500 per 100,000 population per annum.

relations.label: is a treatment for
relations.definition: Adrenaline is used as a treatment for traumatic brain injury.
relations.evidence: A number of reasons have been proposed for these failures which include: poor study design, insufficient dose of drug penetrating the blood brain barrier and inter-species differences in brain injury mechanisms.

relations.label: is monitored in
relations.definition: Patients are monitored in the Intensive Care Unit.
relations.evidence: Collection of minute-by-minute physiological monitoring is now common in many neuro-intensive care units.
